item.title: Mangrove forests are growing back, offering new hope for climate action
item.description: Researchers from Tulane University have observed a significant recovery in mangrove forests worldwide and their role in climate mitigation. After significant losses from 1984 to 2010, net gains have emerged since then due to natural regeneration and restoration efforts. Coastal areas are experiencing this recovery, particularly in regions like the Mississippi River Delta. Healthy mangrove forests can mitigate climate change by accumulating carbon and protecting coastlines. Fuente: The Times of India - World.

item.title: Deadly virus reduces tree frog population by 83% in Atlantic Forest reserve
item.description: A highly lethal pathogen is responsible for the mass death of tadpoles and the rapid decline of amphibian populations in the Atlantic Forest. A group of researchers demonstrate for the first time in South America that recurring ranavirus outbreaks caused an 83% drop in monkey frog (Phyllomedusa distincta) reproduction in a pond in the Brazilian state of Santa Catarina. The disease is caused by a virus that affects reptiles and fish as well. Fuente: Phys.org.

item.description: While mostly accurate describing simple facts, models pivoted to denial and wrong answers when challenged Cop31 live – latest updates Artificial intelligence models can quickly turn into climate crisis deniers at the mildest challenge from users, according to a new UN-backed study. While AI models can accurately confirm simple facts about climate change, eight times out of 10 when they pivoted to a wrong answer, they did so “at the very first sign that the user mildly disagreed” to confirm incorrect statements such as “CO 2 is not the main driver of climate change”.
